utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: D2B. D2B. [Open session] And then, additionally, there was a Prosecution's application for variation of protective measures. The decision of the Chamber reads as follows: Trial Chamber II of the International Tribunal for the Prosecution of Persons Responsible for Serious Violations of International Humanitarian Law Committed in the Territory of the Former Yugoslavia since 1991 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters kindly ask you to slow down when reading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry about this. I thought you had it before you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Are we in open session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: No. No, we are not in open session, and we Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. should continue, as I mentioned before, because we are still discussing issues of closed session. I go on: Being seised of the oral application made by the Office of the Prosecutor, the Prosecution, in the case of Prosecutor versus Milomir Stakic, on 22nd April, 2002, in open session in which the Prosecution requested, on behalf of the Prosecution in the case of Prosecutor versus Brdjanin and Talic, to release the transcripts related to protected Witness A ("Protected Materials") who testified in closed session, to the Defence in the case of Prosecutor versus Brdjanin and Talic ("Application") in order that Witness A's transcript be admitted in that case pursuant to Rule 92 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the International Tribunal ("Rules"), noting that the Defence for Milomir Stakic ("Defence") did not have any objection to this application, noting that Witness A did not have any objections to this procedure, considering that Rule 75(D) of the Rules states in part that: "Once protective measures have been ordered in respect of a victim or witness, a party seeking to vary or rescind such an order must: (I) apply to the Chamber that granted such measures to vary or rescind them or to authorise release of protected material for use in other proceedings." Noting that the Prosecution did not seek to have the protected materials released to "another Chamber" but rather directly to the Defence for the accused Radoslav Brdjanin and Momir Talic. Recalling the "Order on Prosecution's Motion for Particular Protective Measures" ("Order") issued by this Trial Chamber on 29 January 2002, in which the Trial Chamber granted Witness A, who was among other witnesses listed in paragraph 9 of the original Prosecution motion the following protective measures: 1. The Trial Chamber shall assign pseudonyms. 2. The pseudonyms assigned by the Trial Chamber shall be used throughout the course of the trial in the present matter as well as in other proceedings before the International Tribunal if the testimony of the witnesses bearing the pseudonyms is disclosed into those proceedings. 4. [sic] The witnesses identified in paragraph 9 of the motion shall each testify in closed session without a pseudonym. 5. The Defence shall maintain a log of persons who for the purpose of preparing and presenting this case receive from the Defence any information regarding the witnesses identified in paragraph 7, 9 of the motion, but such information shall in no circumstance include the names, addresses, or whereabouts of identifying data of those witnesses. 6. In addition to and in connection with the measure indicated in order 5 above, the Defence shall cause any person who receives the information to sign a Non-disclosure Agreement the format of which is set out in Appendix A of the said Motion and the Trial Chamber shall be informed regularly of such agreements. 7. All hearings to consider the issue of protective measures for the witnesses identified in paragraph 7, 9 of the Motion shall be in closed session. 8. The names, addresses, whereabouts, or other identifying data of the witnesses identified in paragraph 7, 9 of the motion shall remain sealed from the date of issuance of this order and be expunged from documents of the international if they are still there. 9. If a member of the Defence team withdraws from the case, all materials he or she obtains through the disclosure process shall be returned to the lead counsel. 10. The public and media shall not photograph, video-record, or sketch the witnesses identified in paragraphs 7, 9 of the motion while they are on the premises of the International Tribunal. 11. Any rule 92 bis statements of the witnesses identified in paragraph 7 and 9 of the motion shall be kept confidential. The Prosecution is authorised to release the testimony as well as the identities of the witnesses identified in paragraph 7 and 9 of the motion to other Trial Chambers in related cases pending before the International Tribunal. And 13. In the course of implementing order 12 above, the same degree of protection as specified in this order or a lesser degree of protection to which a witnesses expressly consents shall be sought by the Prosecution from the relevant Trial Chambers in related cases. This order does not, however, affect the exercise of powers by those Trial Chambers to balance the rights of the accused with the protection of victims and witnesses in the light of the prevailing circumstances of the other case before them. Considering that the Order in (12) explicitly authorises the Prosecution to release the testimony as well as the identities of the witnesses covered by the order, including Witness A,"to other Trial Chambers in related cases before the International Tribunal", considering that the Order specifically envisioned situations such as the present Application, as reflected in (12) and (13), and that the relief sought in the Application is already provided for in the Order, considering that it is for the "other Trial Chamber" to use of the transcript in another case. Hereby takes the opportunity to inform its instructions in the order with respect to (11) to (13), as stated above, and particularly the Order that the testimony may be released to other Trial Chambers. And reminds the Prosecution of its obligations in seeking the same degree of protection for this witness as stated in the Order, including closed session from the Trial Chamber in which it seeks to offer the protected materials, or, in the event that it seeks a lesser degree of protection, that the Prosecution obtains the express consent of the witness. This is the wording of the decision. Are there any other issues to be discussed in closed session? Then we proceed in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Any contributions from the parties?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: No. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: From the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then we can take it that we proceed tomorrow in the afternoon with Dr. Donia?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We are ready to proceed tomorrow, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: With Dr. Donia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Expert witness, Dr. Donia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Your client wanted to make any comment?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Will you ask him?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It's for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Only we have one issue after we have finished with the official work, to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The next witness will appear when -- in order to find out which time limit we have for tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: The witness would actually be available tomorrow afternoon. I don't know that we're going to -- that the Defence will finish with the cross-examination and whatever questions the Chamber has for the witness, but he's available tomorrow or the next day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Ostojic will be cross-examining Mr. Donia, so I really don't know how long will it take, because right now Mr. Ostojic is flying from the US to Den Haag, so I didn't have time to contact him and to ask how long would it take.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So, in principle, we all are prepared, if possible, to start the hearing of next witness, which is number --?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Witness number 29.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Protective measures. Not closed session, but has protective measures. And I'd also -- I know that it has -- he has facial, or she, has facial distortion, so we'll need a little time with that witness to set it up with the video people before they testify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for this information. And then we adjourn for today --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. If you have only one minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Maybe you don't know, but on the 3rd of May, it's a Good Friday in Orthodox Christianity, and we ask only this Chamber -- you don't have to rule today -- to consider to have a day off, because probably we would be the only Chamber working on that day, because none of the other chambers would work on that Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I can already answer today. It's only one Chamber for specific reasons not going on with the trial. In principle, it is -- the Rule that we have only to obey those holidays which are official United Nations holidays, and the 3rd of May is not such a holiday. Therefore, it would be necessary to demonstrate that there are special religious reasons from the side of your client, or yourself, to depart from this Rule. Therefore, and to add, this was one of the reasons that I prepared already the entire schedule until August 3, to know if there would be such objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At this time, I have to admit that I didn't know that Good Friday is on the 3rd of May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So please take it as it is. If there are no really special and convincing reasons, we will proceed also the 3rd of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thanks a lot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We adjourn and resume tomorrow afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
